title: Sejong the Great
summary: Sejong (1397–1450) was the fourth king of Korea's Joseon dynasty, reigning from 1418 to 1450. He founded the Jiphyeonjeon research institute in 1420, and the sources credit him with the Korean alphabet created in 1443 and promulgated in 1446, and with overseeing instruments such as rain gauges.

uncertainty.note: Reign start is given as August 1418 (Sejong Center) or 1418 (World History Encyclopedia); only life years are used as the span.

where.modern_name: Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu, Seoul (proxy for his birthplace near Yeongchunmun Gate of the palace)
where.historical_name: Jungsubang, Hanyang, Joseon Korea (birthplace, per the Sejong Center)

importance.justification: Monarch credited by the sources with creating the Korean alphabet and sponsoring scientific instruments.
